key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating interface-driven failure from bulk effects.
engineering_relevance: The method helps engineers identify the dominant degradation site in a working device, enabling more targeted materials design and passivation strategies for longer-lived solar cells.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optical data
Bayesian inference to infer spatial maps of recombination-related parameters over aging time
evidence_signal: The abstract reports time-resolved inferred parameter maps during aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight, revealing spatially non-uniform degradation and clear suppression after amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The inferred degradation attribution depends on the fidelity of the optical model and simulation assumptions, so mismatches between model and real device physics could bias localization.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
